details: Knowledge stored in the model's weights vs. knowledge fetched at inference time from external sources (RAG, tools, databases). Production systems deliberately shift factual load to the non-parametric side because it is updatable, auditable, and citable.

explainer.lead: Parametric knowledge is stored in the model's weights; non-parametric knowledge is fetched at inference time from external sources such as RAG, tools, or databases. The split matters because production systems deliberately shift factual load to the non-parametric side, which is updatable, auditable, and citable.

tiers.eli5: Some facts are baked into the model's memory, like things you memorized; others it looks up on the spot, like checking a reference book.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers route volatile or high-stakes facts to retrieval and tools instead of relying on weights alone. A pitfall is that weight-stored facts cannot be updated or cited without retraining, so stale or unsourced answers slip through if retrieval is skipped.
tiers.paperLevel: Knowledge stored in the model's weights (parametric) versus knowledge fetched at inference time from external sources such as RAG, tools, and databases (non-parametric); production systems deliberately shift factual load to the non-parametric side because it is updatable, auditable, and citable.

explainer.example: A support assistant answers policy questions by retrieving the current policy document at inference time rather than relying on what the model memorized during training.
